Plot survey responses as a serpentine band per item

Source: R/survey_snake.R
survey_snake.Rd

survey_snake() draws a survey snake plot, which shows the distribution of responses to a set of rating items, one band per item, with consecutive items joined by U-turns so that a long instrument fits in one panel in its item order. Each band shows every response as a tick placed in the zone of its response level, the item mean as a diamond, and a shade running from warm (low mean) to cool (high mean). The display shows how responses are spread on each item and how the items compare.

The function accepts raw responses (one row per respondent, one column per item), a table of counts (one row per item, one column per response level), or experience-sampling data in long format, where var and day make each day a band and timestamp places each response at its time of day. Responses can be drawn as lines, jittered dots, or a stacked bar with percentages. The U-turns can carry the Pearson correlation between the two items they join (arc_fill = "correlation"); this needs raw responses, because a table of counts does not record which respondent gave which answer. With facet, groups of items are drawn as separate panels. It returns the layout invisibly as a snake_layout object, or a list of them with facet.

For a compact 100% stacked bar per item use survey_sequence(), or sequential_dist() for scales without a neutral midpoint. Palettes for the response levels are given by snake_palette().

Usage

survey_snake(
  counts,
  labels = NULL,
  levels = NULL,
  var = NULL,
  day = NULL,
  timestamp = NULL,
  level_labels = NULL,
  band_height = 28,
  band_gap = 18,
  plot_width = 500,
  tick_shape = c("line", "dot", "bar"),
  bar_reverse = FALSE,
  tick_opacity = 0.75,
  level_gap = 15,
  color_mode = c("level", "individual"),
  colors = NULL,
  shade_band = TRUE,
  show_mean = TRUE,
  show_median = FALSE,
  show_correlation = TRUE,
  jitter_range = 0.22,
  sort_by = c("none", "mean", "net"),
  shadow = TRUE,
  label_color = "#333333",
  label_size = 0.85,
  label_align = "left",
  show_legend = TRUE,
  legend_text_size = 0.65,
  arc_color = "#2c3e6b",
  arc_opacity = 0.8,
  arc_fill = c("none", "correlation", "mean_prev", "blend"),
  band_palette = NULL,
  start_from = c("left", "right"),
  flow = c("snake", "natural"),
  facet = FALSE,
  facet_ncol = 2L,
  title = NULL,
  margin = c(top = 30, right = 10, bottom = 55, left = 100),
  background = "white",
  seed = 42L
)

Arguments

counts

Responses, in one of four forms:

  • a data frame of raw responses, one row per respondent and one column per item;

  • a numeric matrix of counts, items in rows and response levels in columns;

  • a data frame of counts, converted to a matrix;

  • a long data frame of experience-sampling responses, used with var and day.

A data frame is read as raw responses when its columns hold few distinct whole-number or categorical values relative to its number of rows, and as counts otherwise.

labels

Item labels, one per item. NULL (default) uses the row names of a count table, or, for raw responses, the column names with the number of responses.

levels

Response levels in scale order. NULL (default) uses the column names of a count table, or, for raw responses, the factor levels or the sorted distinct values. For raw responses the levels must match the values in the data; use level_labels to relabel them.

var, day, timestamp

Column names for experience-sampling data in long format: the response variable, the day (or other period) that defines each band, and optionally a POSIXct timestamp that places each response at its time of day. Bands are labelled "Day 1", "Day 2", and so on, and title defaults to var.

level_labels

Display labels for the response levels: a vector named by level, such as c("1" = "Never", "5" = "Always"), or an unnamed vector with one label per level.

band_height, band_gap

Height of each band and gap between bands, in plot units (defaults 28 and 18).

plot_width

Length of each band in plot units (default 500).

tick_shape

"line" (default), "dot" (jittered points) or "bar" (a stacked bar with percentages).

bar_reverse

For tick_shape = "bar", draw the highest level first (default FALSE).

tick_opacity

Opacity of the ticks, between 0 and 1 (default 0.75).

level_gap

Gap, in plot units, between the zones of adjacent response levels (default 15; 0 for none).

color_mode

"level" (default) colors each tick by its response level; "individual" gives every tick its own hue.

colors

One color per response level, in scale order. Only the first length(levels) colors are used, so pass snake_palette(name, n = <number of levels>). NULL (default) uses a red-to-blue diverging palette.

shade_band

Has no effect at present: the band is always shaded by the item mean.

show_mean

Draw a diamond at the item mean (default TRUE).

show_median

Draw a dashed line at the item median (default FALSE).

show_correlation

With arc_fill = "correlation", print the correlation at each U-turn (default TRUE).

jitter_range

For tick_shape = "dot", vertical scatter of the points as a fraction of half the band height (default 0.22).

sort_by

Order of the items: "none" (default, input order), "mean" (increasing item mean) or "net" (increasing share of responses above the middle level minus share below; the mean for scales with fewer than four levels).

shadow

Draw drop shadows (default TRUE).

label_color, label_size

Color and size multiplier of the item labels (defaults "#333333" and 0.85).

label_align

Alignment of the item labels: "left" (default), "right", or "direction" to follow each band's reading direction.

show_legend

Draw the legend (default TRUE).

legend_text_size

Size of the legend text (default 0.65).

arc_color

Color of the U-turns for a positive correlation when arc_fill = "correlation"; a negative correlation uses its complement (default "#2c3e6b").

arc_opacity

Opacity of the U-turns for arc_fill = "mean_prev" and "blend", and of U-turns without a correlation (default 0.80).

arc_fill

Fill of the U-turns: "none" (default) continues the shades of the two bands it joins; "correlation" tints it by the Pearson correlation between the two items, darker for a larger absolute value; "mean_prev" uses the shade of the preceding item; "blend" mixes the two shades.

band_palette

Two or more colors for the band shade, from low to high item mean. NULL (default) uses a dark brown-to-slate ramp.

start_from

Side on which the first band starts: "left" (default) or "right".

flow

"snake" (default): bands alternate direction. "natural": every band reads in the same direction.

facet

FALSE (default) for one panel. TRUE groups the columns of raw responses by name prefix (LOC1, LOC2 become LOC; Emo_Happy becomes Emo) and draws one panel per group, with the prefix removed from the item labels and one shared legend in a spare panel. A named list of column-name vectors gives the groups explicitly.

facet_ncol

Number of panel columns for facet (default 2).

title

Plot title, or NULL (default) for none.

margin

Named numeric vector of top, right, bottom and left margins in plot units (default c(top = 30, right = 10, bottom = 55, left = 100)).

background

Background color (default "white").

seed

Seed for the random placement of ticks within their zones (default 42), so the same call draws the same plot. The session's random number state is restored when the function returns.

Value

The plot is drawn on the current device. The function returns, invisibly, an object of class snake_layout: a list describing the drawn geometry, with bands (a data frame with one row per item band and columns i, y_center, y_top, y_bottom, x_left, x_right, direction and read_direction), arcs (a list with one element per U-turn), canvas and plot_area (dimensions in plot units), orientation, flow and params (the sizes used).

With arc_fill = "correlation" the list also holds correlations, a data frame with one row per U-turn and columns from and to (the item names), r (the Pearson correlation over the respondents who answered both items; NA when fewer than three did or either item is constant among them) and n (the number of those respondents). With other arc_fill values the list has no correlations component. as.data.frame() returns these tables.

With facet, a named list of such objects, one per panel.

Conditions

An error of class snakeplot_no_respondent_data when arc_fill = "correlation" and counts is a table of counts or var and day are given.

See also

as.data.frame.snake_layout() for the tables of the returned layout; survey_sequence() and sequential_dist() for stacked bars; snake_palette() for level colors; ema_emotions, student_survey and ema_beeps for example data.

Examples

# Raw responses: 280 students, ten emotion items rated 1-5
survey_snake(ema_emotions, sort_by = "mean")


# Correlations between adjacent items on the U-turns
survey_snake(ema_emotions, arc_fill = "correlation", tick_shape = "dot")


# Experience sampling: one band per study day, responses at their time
survey_snake(ema_beeps, var = "happy", day = "day",
             timestamp = "start_time")


# A table of counts with named levels
counts <- matrix(c(110, 210, 79,  84, 42,
                   126, 205, 68, 100, 26,
                   184, 226, 47,  58, 10),
                 nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,
                 dimnames = list(c("LOC1", "LOC2", "LOC3"),
                                 c("Never", "Rarely", "Sometimes",
                                   "Often", "Always")))
survey_snake(counts, tick_shape = "bar",
             colors = snake_palette("earth", n = 5))


# One panel per group of items
survey_snake(student_survey, facet = TRUE, tick_shape = "bar")
